h1: 10XBNB Alternatives: Six Airbnb Arbitrage Programs Compared
verdict: 10XBNB is a reasonable buy if you want arbitrage and co-hosting taught side by side in a self-paced library, with a large active group and live calls. It is a weaker fit if you want one named coach who reads your lease and runs the numbers on a specific deal before you sign, or if you want to test the model cheaply before committing. Those are the two reasons most people search for alternatives, and they point to different programs.

Our own program, Airbnb Ascension, is on this list and we say so wherever it appears. It fits the one-coach, one-property, done-with-you buyer. If you are self-directed and want a refundable first step, Sean Rakidzich's self-paced courses are a better starting point than either 10XBNB or Ascension. If you want to buy rather than lease, skip all three arbitrage programs and read the acquisition options further down.

competitorProfile.what: 10XBNB is an Airbnb coaching brand founded by Shaun Ghavami and Ari Rahmanian. It teaches three ways to earn from short-term rentals without owning property: rental arbitrage (lease a unit, furnish it, sublet it nightly), bed flipping (renting by the room or bed), and co-listing, which is its name for co-hosting someone else's listing for a share of the revenue.
competitorProfile.format: Self-paced video modules, an active private Facebook group, and live group coaching calls. Pricing is not published on the program, FAQ or reviews pages we checked; the FAQ sends you to a contact page. Verify the current offering on 10xbnb.com before you buy, because module lists, call schedules and inclusions change without notice.

whereLisFits: Airbnb Ascension is the right pick when you want one person accountable to you and one property finished. The 6-month program gives you a dedicated coach, a Market Matrix to pick the city, a Property Profitability Report before you sign anything, landlord scripts with roleplay, a coach who will vouch for you with the landlord, and done-for-you listing, furnishing, automation and pricing setup once the lease is signed. The Airbnb Arbitrage Roadmap curriculum underneath it is about 7 hours of video with lifetime access; the rest of the program is people and process.

The results we can point to are on our reviews page, not in a sales deck. Tom, after a corporate layoff, booked $25,000 in reservations in his first two weeks and reports $5,000 to $6,000 a month in cash flow from his first Chesapeake Bay property. Kiana left a ten-year finance career, runs two Scottsdale arbitrage units at about $3,200 a month in cash flow, and quit her job three months in. These are individual outcomes, not a promise; your market, your capital and your speed decide yours. Our Trustpilot profile shows a 4.2 TrustScore from 66 reviews as of September 2026, and the one-star reviews are published alongside the five-star ones.
whereLisDoesNotFit: Ascension is the wrong first step if you want to test the idea cheaply, because pricing is not published, there is no published money-back guarantee, and the program assumes you bring your own working capital for deposits and furniture. It is also the wrong fit if you want more than one property in six months on the standard term, or if you want co-hosting as your starting point rather than a later add-on.

It is also not for buyers. One of our own students, Jeff, chose to buy his Galveston property after 28 years in banking and reports $7,000 to $8,000 a month after his mortgage. That is a different program and a different tax picture from leasing. If ownership is your goal, read the short-term rental loophole page and an acquisition-focused course before you talk to us or to 10XBNB.
howToDecide: Check your target city's short-term rental rules first. If stays under 30 days are banned where you can afford to lease, no program on this page helps.
Decide lease or buy. Arbitrage gives cash flow without equity; ownership gives equity, depreciation and the short-term rental tax rules but needs a down payment.
Decide co-hosting first or arbitrage first. If co-hosting, 10XBNB's curriculum covers it as a core path. If arbitrage with a coach, Ascension. If arbitrage alone, Rakidzich.
Count your reserve. If a program fee would use up the money you need for deposits and furniture, buy the cheap course and keep the cash.
Ask every seller the same four questions in writing: what is the price, what is the refund policy, who exactly coaches me, and will you review my specific lease before I sign it.

Pick on format, not on brand size. A big group suits some people; a single coach with same-day messaging suits others.

faqs.q: Is 10XBNB legit?
faqs.a: 10XBNB is an operating coaching company with public program pages, an active student community and live group calls. Whether it is the right buy for you is a different question. Ask for the price and refund terms in writing, ask who coaches you and how often, and ask whether anyone reviews your specific lease before you sign. Judge any program, including ours, by those answers.

faqs.q: How much does 10XBNB cost?
faqs.a: 10XBNB does not publish a price on its program, FAQ or reviews pages. The FAQ sends you to a contact page, so the number comes on a call. Airbnb Ascension does not publish a price either; it is discussed on the strategy call. If you want a published price before you talk to anyone, Sean Rakidzich's self-paced courses are the option on this page that provides one.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 10XBNB and Airbnb Ascension?
faqs.a: 10XBNB teaches arbitrage, bed flipping and co-listing through self-paced modules, a Facebook group and live group calls. Airbnb Ascension is a 6-month, one-property arbitrage program with a dedicated 1-on-1 coach, a Property Profitability Report on each deal before you sign, a coach who will act as a landlord reference, and done-for-you listing, furnishing, automation and pricing setup. The short version: 10XBNB is a broader library; Ascension is narrower and more hands-on.

faqs.q: What is the best alternative to 10XBNB?
faqs.a: It depends on why you are leaving. If you want a coach who reviews your lease and a landlord reference, Airbnb Ascension. If you want a cheap, refundable first step, Sean Rakidzich's courses. If you want to buy rather than lease, an acquisition-focused course plus the short-term rental tax rules. If you want free, BiggerPockets forums and YouTube.

faqs.q: Does 10XBNB teach co-hosting?
faqs.a: Yes. Co-listing is its term for co-hosting, and it is one of the three models in the program alongside arbitrage and bed flipping. Airbnb Ascension includes a co-hosting masterclass as a scaling resource, but the program itself is built around leasing one property. If co-hosting is your primary plan, 10XBNB's curriculum is the closer fit.

faqs.q: Can I do Airbnb arbitrage without a course?
faqs.a: Yes. The steps are public: check local rules, pick a market, find a landlord who will put sublet permission in writing, furnish, list, price and automate. What a course sells is sequencing, templates and accountability, and what a coached program sells is a person who checks your numbers and vouches for you. If you are disciplined and have time, YouTube plus a spreadsheet can get you there. Most people who stall do so at the landlord step, not the knowledge step.

faqs.q: Do 10XBNB or Airbnb Ascension offer a money-back guarantee?
faqs.a: We found no guarantee published on the 10XBNB pages we checked, and Airbnb Ascension does not publish one. Sean Rakidzich publishes a 30-day money-back guarantee on his courses. Whatever you buy, get the refund policy in writing before you pay.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to start Airbnb arbitrage?
faqs.a: Separate from any program cost, our guidance is roughly $10,000 to $25,000 of working capital for a first unit: security deposit, first month's rent, furniture and a reserve for a slow first quarter. Some markets need less, some more. Run your target unit through our arbitrage ROI calculator before you commit to anything.

faqs.q: How is Airbnb arbitrage income taxed?
faqs.a: Arbitrage is a business you operate, not a property you own. Your nightly revenue is business income, and your rent, furniture, supplies, cleaning, software and platform fees are business expenses. Because you do not own the building, there is no building to depreciate and no cost segregation to run. Most of the tax planning that applies is entity choice, deductions and record keeping. Talk to a tax professional about your facts; this is education, not advice.

faqs.q: Does the short-term rental loophole apply to Airbnb arbitrage?
faqs.a: Generally no. The short-term rental loophole lets an owner who materially participates treat rental losses, often created by depreciation and cost segregation, as non-passive so they can offset other income such as W-2 wages. An arbitrage operator does not own the property, so there is no depreciation to create that loss. If that tax outcome is your main goal, ownership is the model to study, not arbitrage.

faqs.q: What is the difference between BNB Formula and Airbnb Ascension?
faqs.a: Both teach rental arbitrage. BNB Formula is a large, long-running brand whose public pages lead with a free book and a call; the coaching format is not detailed publicly. Airbnb Ascension is a 6-month, one-property program with a dedicated 1-on-1 coach, a Property Profitability Report before you sign, a coach who acts as a landlord reference, done-for-you setup after the lease, and a tax and entity session. Neither publishes a price or a money-back guarantee.

faqs.q: Should I lease or buy my first short-term rental?
faqs.a: Lease if you want cash flow quickly with a smaller capital outlay and you are comfortable owing rent in a slow month. Buy if you have a down payment, want equity, and want the depreciation and short-term rental tax rules that only owners get. Some of our students have done each; Tom and Kiana leased, Jeff bought. Run both through a calculator before you choose a program.
